nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives grass growth across the open prairie through the warm season.

nodes.name: Rain & snowmelt
nodes.desc: Limited rainfall is what makes this a mixed-grass prairie, with grasses from ankle to waist height.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: Prairie fire clears dead growth and keeps trees and shrubs from spreading across the grassland.

nodes.name: Prairie soil & badland clays
nodes.desc: Soils on the benches hold the grass roots; the eroding badland slopes stay mostly bare.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Western wheatgrass
nodes.desc: A sod-forming perennial grass and South Dakota's state grass. Bison and prairie dogs eat it.

nodes.name: Blue grama
nodes.desc: A short prairie grass that prairie dogs eat in spring and summer.

nodes.name: Plains prickly pear
nodes.desc: A spiny cactus of dry ground. Prairie dogs eat it in winter and draw water from it.

nodes.name: Moss-rose
nodes.desc: A low orange-flowered wildflower of dry prairie that prairie dogs favour in late summer and fall.

nodes.name: American bison
nodes.desc: About 50 bison were released in 1963 and the herd has grown to over 1,200. They graze grasses such as western wheatgrass.

nodes.name: Black-tailed prairie dog
nodes.desc: Eats mostly grasses and is called an ecosystem engineer. Its colonies feed and shelter ferrets and burrowing owls.

nodes.name: Pronghorn
nodes.desc: A fast grazing and browsing animal of open plains, listed among the park's mammals.

nodes.name: Bighorn sheep
nodes.desc: Lives on the steep badland slopes, where the park's population has reached 233.

nodes.name: Desert cottontail
nodes.desc: A small rabbit that eats grasses and herbs and is prey for many predators.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: A small seed and insect eater that many mammals, birds and snakes hunt.

nodes.name: Burrowing owl
nodes.desc: Nests underground and is associated with prairie dog colonies. Hunts small mammals, birds, frogs and insects.

nodes.name: Black-footed ferret
nodes.desc: Lives in prairie dog burrows and eats mostly prairie dogs. Reintroduced near the park; about 100 live in the park.

nodes.name: American badger
nodes.desc: Digs out prairie dogs and small rodents and is recorded eating burrowing owls.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: Hunts prairie dogs, rabbits, rodents and snakes from the air.

nodes.name: Bullsnake
nodes.desc: A large constrictor that eats rodents, rabbits and ground birds.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Finds carcasses by smell and soaring. Recorded feeding on many of the park's mammals.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: A top predator here. It hunts prairie dogs, pronghorn, rabbits and rodents, and eats badgers and ferrets.
